related_questions.question: What is the best exercise for arthritic hands?

text_blocks.snippet: Gentle exercises like making a fist, finger bends, and finger lifts can help improve hand strength and flexibility for those with arthritic hands. Other helpful exercises include thumb stretches, making an "O" shape with your fingers, and knuckle bends according to AICA Orthopedics.
snippet_highlighted_words: making a fist, finger bends, and finger lifts

list.snippet: Making a Fist: Extend your hand flat, then slowly curl your fingers into a fist and release.
Finger Bends: Hold your hand out with fingers straight, then slowly bend each finger towards your palm individually.
Finger Lifts: Place your hand flat on a table and lift one finger at a time.
Make an "O" Shape: Extend your hand and bring your thumb to each fingertip, forming an "O" shape.
Knuckle Bends: In a high-five position, bend the fingers at the main knuckle and then straighten.
Thumb Stretch: Extend your thumb away from your hand and hold, then release.
Fist Stretch: Gently bend your fingers into a fist, then release.
Finger Spreads: Spread your fingers as wide as possible and then close them into a fist according to AARP.
Start slowly and gently: Avoid overexerting your hands and stop if you experience pain.
Breathe deeply: Inhale and exhale slowly as you move through the exercises.
Be consistent: Perform these exercises regularly to maintain or improve hand function says the Arthritis Foundation.
Consult with a healthcare professional: If you have any concerns or experience persistent pain, seek advice from your doctor or a physical therapist recommends the Mayo Clinic.

related_questions.question: Does squeezing a ball help arthritis?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, squeezing a ball, like a stress ball or therapy ball, can be a helpful exercise for managing arthritis in the hands. It can improve hand strength and flexibility, which can be beneficial for individuals with arthritis. However, it's important to be gentle and stop if it causes pain, according to Medical News Today.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, squeezing a ball, like a stress ball or therapy ball, can be a helpful exercise for managing arthritis in the hands

text_blocks.snippet: Benefits of Squeezing a Ball for Arthritis:

list.title: Increased strength:
list.snippet: Squeezing a ball can help strengthen the muscles in your hands and forearms, which can make daily tasks easier.

list.title: Improved flexibility:
list.snippet: The repetitive motion of squeezing and releasing can help improve the range of motion in your fingers and wrists.

list.title: Reduced pain and stiffness:
list.snippet: Gentle hand exercises, like squeezing a ball, can help reduce stiffness and pain associated with arthritis.

list.title: Enhanced grip strength:
list.snippet: Stronger hand muscles can improve your ability to grip objects, which can be helpful for those with arthritis.

list.title: Mindfulness:
list.snippet: Focusing on the exercise can also be a form of mindfulness, helping to relieve stress and tension.

text_blocks.snippet: Tips for Squeezing a Ball for Arthritis:

list.snippet: Choose the right ball: Start with a soft ball and gradually progress to a firmer one as your strength improves.
Be gentle: Avoid squeezing too hard, especially when starting out.
Listen to your body: Stop if you feel any pain.
Consistency is key: Incorporate this exercise into your daily routine for the best results.

Consult with a healthcare professional: Before starting any new exercise routine, it's always a good idea to consult with your doctor or physical therapist, especially if you have pre-existing conditions.

text_blocks.snippet: Besides squeezing a ball, there are other exercises that can be helpful for managing arthritis in the hands, such as:

list.snippet: Making a fist and holding it for a few seconds.
Finger lifts and stretches.
Thumb exercises, like thumb bends and stretches.
Wrist bends and rotations.
Using therapy putty for resistance exercises.
